neighbours.label: the first piece of 'giggle', 'nibble' or 'tremble' (' gig', ' nib', ' trem' as the stem of the verb, not the nouns gig or nib)
fire: The twins started to giggle at the back of the church.
A rabbit came out to nibble the lettuce in the garden.
She tried to hide a giggle behind her hand.
His voice began to tremble as he read the letter.
The goats nibbled on the hedge all afternoon.
The children heard a giggle from under the bed.
Guests were offered drinks and a few nibbles before dinner.
Her lip trembled when she heard the news.
quiet: The twins started to whisper at the back of the church.
A rabbit came out to eat the lettuce in the garden.
She tried to hide a chuckle behind her hand.
His voice began to shake as he read the letter.
The goats grazed along the hedge all afternoon.
The singer has a gig in Leeds on Friday.
He dipped the nib of his pen into the ink.
The old bridge began to wobble under the lorry.

notes: Card: peaks on ' nib'(ble), ' gig'(gle), ' trem'(ulous), NIB(IRU). Probes: giggle 0.47 and 0.89, nibble(d) 0.38 and 0.46, tremble 0.30, tremulous 0.13; pen 'nib' 0.03, a 'gig' at a pub 0.00, gigabytes 0.00, wobble/scribble/juggle/chuckle 0.01-0.03. A list of three stems; I did not find a shared pattern that extends to other -ble/-gle verbs.
